title: NEXT F Security Control Registry
description: Machine-readable security standards for NEXT F platform surfaces.

categories.label: Session Management
categories.description: Session creation, rotation, expiry and revocation.

categories.label: Authorization
categories.description: Permission evaluation and privileged operation controls.

categories.label: Browser Security
categories.description: CSRF, XSS, sanitization, redirects and browser execution boundaries.

categories.label: API & Service Security
categories.description: CORS, rate limits, service authentication and safe API boundaries.

categories.label: Secrets & Credentials
categories.description: Secrets, API keys, OAuth credentials and token handling.

categories.label: File Uploads
categories.description: Upload type, size, scanning, storage and download safety.

categories.label: Abuse Prevention
categories.description: Rate limiting, brute force and automated abuse resistance.

categories.label: Logging & Audit
categories.description: Security logging, auditability and safe error behavior.

categories.label: Transport & Headers
categories.description: TLS, HTTPS, CSP and security headers.

categories.label: Dependency & Supply Chain
categories.description: Dependency hygiene and build artifact integrity.

categories.label: Personal Data Security
categories.description: Security handling for personal and sensitive information.

categories.label: Webhook Security
categories.description: Endpoint security, signing, replay resistance and delivery trust.

controls.name: Abuse prevention
controls.requirement: Forms, authentication and other abuse-prone surfaces must apply layered controls appropriate to risk without treating one signal as authoritative.
controls.rationale: Automated abuse can bypass simple client-side checks.

controls.name: Audit privileged changes
controls.requirement: Security-relevant and privileged state changes must produce sufficient audit evidence to identify actor, action, scope, outcome and time.
controls.rationale: Privileged actions need traceability and incident-review evidence.

controls.name: Authentication required for protected operations
controls.requirement: Protected and privileged operations must require an authenticated principal using an approved authentication mechanism.
controls.rationale: Unauthenticated access must never be treated as sufficient proof of identity.

controls.name: Recent authentication for high-risk actions
controls.requirement: High-risk operations that declare recent-authentication requirements must re-establish sufficiently recent user authentication before execution.
controls.rationale: Long-lived sessions must not silently authorize sensitive account or credential changes.

controls.name: Server-side permission enforcement
controls.requirement: Every privileged operation must enforce canonical permissions at the server boundary; UI visibility is never the authorization decision.
controls.rationale: Client-side controls are bypassable and cannot protect authoritative state.

controls.name: Privileged operation confirmation
controls.requirement: Destructive or privileged operations must apply the confirmation and recent-authentication requirements declared by their operational metadata.
controls.rationale: High-impact operations require explicit user intent and policy enforcement.

controls.name: Contract-data backup
controls.requirement: Authoritative contract source and critical registry release artifacts must be recoverable from version-controlled or otherwise verified backups.
controls.rationale: Loss or silent corruption of contract authority would affect every consumer.

controls.name: Brute-force resistance
controls.requirement: Authentication and sensitive verification flows must limit repeated attempts and support lockout/backoff or equivalent defenses without exposing account-enumeration details.
controls.rationale: Repeated guessing attacks target credentials and verification factors.

controls.name: Explicit CORS policy
controls.requirement: APIs must apply the canonical CORS policy appropriate to their surface and must not use permissive credentialed cross-origin access.
controls.rationale: Cross-origin access must be deliberate and least-privileged.

controls.name: Content Security Policy
controls.requirement: Web applications should use a restrictive, deployment-appropriate CSP and integrations must not silently weaken it with uncontrolled script origins.
controls.rationale: CSP limits the blast radius of injection and third-party script compromise.

controls.name: CSRF protection for browser-authenticated writes
controls.requirement: Browser-authenticated state-changing requests must use CSRF-resistant request patterns and must not rely on ambient credentials alone.
controls.rationale: Cross-site requests must not be able to trigger privileged mutations.

controls.name: Dependency vulnerability management
controls.requirement: Runtime and build dependencies must be inventoried, reviewed and updated when security risk requires it.
controls.rationale: Known vulnerable dependencies can compromise otherwise-correct application code.

controls.name: Environment isolation
controls.requirement: Development, preview/staging and production environments must keep credentials, data access and integrations appropriately isolated.
controls.rationale: Environment crossover can expose production data or credentials.

controls.name: Customer-safe error handling
controls.requirement: Errors returned to untrusted clients must not expose secrets, stack traces, internal credentials, private paths or cross-tenant data.
controls.rationale: Verbose internal failures can disclose exploitable implementation detail.

controls.name: Security headers baseline
controls.requirement: Web surfaces must apply security headers appropriate to their runtime, including framing, content-type and referrer protections where applicable.
controls.rationale: Browser security headers provide defense-in-depth against common web attacks.

controls.name: Replay-safe idempotency for sensitive commands
controls.requirement: Sensitive retried commands must use contract-defined idempotency/replay protections where duplicate execution could alter security or financial state.
controls.rationale: Retries and replay can otherwise duplicate privileged or financial effects.

controls.name: Authoritative server input validation
controls.requirement: All untrusted input must be validated server-side against the relevant canonical contract before authoritative use.
controls.rationale: Client validation is UX only and cannot establish trust.

controls.name: Integration credential isolation
controls.requirement: Third-party connections must keep provider credentials protected, environment-scoped and separate from customer-visible configuration.
controls.rationale: External providers often grant access beyond one page or request.

controls.name: Integration failure containment
controls.requirement: Optional external providers must not become a trust dependency for primary content and must fail without exposing credentials or bypassing canonical validation.
controls.rationale: Provider outages or malformed responses must not break platform trust boundaries.

controls.name: API key handling
controls.requirement: Private API keys must be stored and transmitted only through protected server-side mechanisms; public identifiers must be distinguished from secret keys.
controls.rationale: Provider keys frequently have broad external authority.

controls.name: Secret-safe logging
controls.requirement: Logs must exclude secrets and credentials and minimize personal data while preserving operational security evidence.
controls.rationale: Logs are broadly retained and accessed and can become a secondary data breach source.

controls.name: OAuth credential and token handling
controls.requirement: OAuth client secrets, access tokens and refresh tokens must remain protected; redirect/callback configuration must be explicit and validated.
controls.rationale: OAuth bearer material grants external-system access.

controls.name: Context-aware output encoding
controls.requirement: Untrusted values must be encoded for the output context in which they are rendered.
controls.rationale: Escaping requirements differ across HTML, attributes, URLs and script-adjacent contexts.

controls.name: No PAN/CVV storage
controls.requirement: NEXT F contracts and implementations must not store raw payment card PAN or CVV; provider tokenization or equivalent provider-hosted handling is required.
controls.rationale: Raw card storage materially expands payment-security scope and is outside the NEXT F model.

controls.name: Server-authoritative payment reconciliation
controls.requirement: Payment, authorization, capture and refund state must be reconciled from trusted server/provider evidence and canonical business invariants; browser-calculated totals or states are never authoritative.
controls.rationale: Financial integrity cannot depend on client-controlled values.

controls.name: Payment/refund authorization
controls.requirement: Payment export/manage and refund creation/management operations must enforce their canonical permissions and business invariants server-side.
controls.rationale: Financial operations require explicit least-privilege authorization.

controls.name: Personal-data security minimization
controls.requirement: Personal data must be collected, exposed, logged, emitted and delivered only when the owning contract and purpose require it, with appropriate authorization.
controls.rationale: Reducing unnecessary exposure reduces breach impact.

controls.name: Preview and staging access control
controls.requirement: Non-production environments containing customer data, privileged previews or production-like integrations must be access-controlled and clearly isolated from public production.
controls.rationale: Preview URLs are not inherently private.

controls.name: Sensitive values excluded from URLs
controls.requirement: Sensitive values must not be placed in query strings or fragments unless an explicit contract permits a narrowly scoped safe token.
controls.rationale: URLs leak through history, logs, referrers and screenshots.

controls.name: Rate limiting
controls.requirement: Public and authenticated endpoints must apply an appropriate canonical rate-limit class based on abuse and resource risk.
controls.rationale: Unbounded request rates enable denial of service and automation abuse.

controls.name: Recovery verification
controls.requirement: Recovery procedures for authoritative contract data must preserve integrity, version identity and auditability rather than restoring an unverifiable latest state.
controls.rationale: A backup is not sufficient if restoration cannot be trusted.

controls.name: Safe redirects
controls.requirement: Redirect destinations derived from input must be constrained to explicitly allowed destinations or validated safe origins.
controls.rationale: Open redirects enable phishing and token leakage.

controls.name: Service-to-service authentication
controls.requirement: Internal service calls that can access protected data or perform privileged operations must authenticate the calling service and authorize the requested scope.
controls.rationale: Network location alone is not identity or authorization.

controls.name: Content sanitization
controls.requirement: Rich or user-supplied content that permits markup must be sanitized according to its contract before trusted rendering.
controls.rationale: Stored or reflected untrusted markup can become executable content.

controls.name: No privileged secrets in public delivery
controls.requirement: Secrets, credentials, tokens, signing secrets and encryption keys must never be embedded in public Site Manifests, browser bundles, public events, examples or unauthenticated responses.
controls.rationale: Public delivery permanently destroys confidentiality.

controls.name: Server-side secret references
controls.requirement: Provider and platform secrets must be represented by protected references rather than raw values in canonical public/configuration contracts.
controls.rationale: References preserve separation between declarative configuration and credential storage.

controls.name: Secure session lifecycle
controls.requirement: Sessions must have bounded lifetime, secure invalidation, rotation where appropriate, and server-authoritative revocation.
controls.rationale: Stale or stolen sessions must not remain indefinitely usable.

controls.name: Server-side outbound request restrictions
controls.requirement: Server-side URL fetching and callback delivery must reject unsafe schemes/targets and apply network policy before connecting.
controls.rationale: Untrusted URLs can otherwise reach internal or privileged network resources.

controls.name: Build and generated-artifact integrity
controls.requirement: Generated contract artifacts and release packages must retain integrity evidence and must not silently diverge from authoritative source.
controls.rationale: Supply-chain integrity protects consumers from tampered or stale generated data.

controls.name: Organization and Site isolation
controls.requirement: Tenant and Site scope must be derived and enforced server-side; browser-supplied tenant identifiers are never proof of authorization.
controls.rationale: Cross-tenant access is a critical platform boundary.

controls.name: HTTPS/TLS required
controls.requirement: Production network communication carrying authenticated, personal, secret or webhook data must use HTTPS/TLS with certificate validation.
controls.rationale: Transport confidentiality and integrity are foundational security properties.

controls.name: Bearer and token exposure prevention
controls.requirement: Bearer/session/access/refresh tokens must not be logged, placed in public content, or exposed in query strings unless an explicit contract safely requires a short-lived token.
controls.rationale: Tokens commonly function as credentials.

controls.name: Upload type and size enforcement
controls.requirement: File uploads must enforce contract-defined allowed media/types and size limits server-side.
controls.rationale: Client-provided filenames and MIME declarations are not trust boundaries.

controls.name: Upload normalization and quarantine
controls.requirement: Upload handling must normalize filenames, restrict executable content, and support scan/quarantine state before risky content becomes available.
controls.rationale: Uploaded files can carry executable or malicious payloads.
subrequirements: Normalize filenames and never trust path components.
Keep private-by-default where the owning contract is private.
Do not serve quarantined content as trusted media.
Distinguish managed media assets from form-submission attachments.

controls.name: Authorized download and safe headers
controls.requirement: Protected uploaded files must require authorization and use safe download/content headers appropriate to the file contract.
controls.rationale: Upload authorization must continue at retrieval time.

controls.name: Webhook endpoint validation
controls.requirement: Webhook destinations must satisfy HTTPS/network-policy validation before activation and must not permit unsafe internal targets.
controls.rationale: Outbound webhooks can become an SSRF path.

controls.name: Webhook signing and secret rotation
controls.requirement: Webhook deliveries requiring authenticity must use the canonical signature policy and protected signing-key references with finite secret-rotation overlap.
controls.rationale: Receivers need verifiable origin without exposing long-lived signing secrets.

controls.name: Webhook replay resistance
controls.requirement: Webhook delivery/verification must apply timestamp, signature and replay-protection rules so captured valid requests cannot be reused outside policy.
controls.rationale: Signed messages can still be replayed if freshness and uniqueness are ignored.

controls.name: No arbitrary script execution from managed content
controls.requirement: CMS/content values must not create arbitrary executable script paths in customer websites or management interfaces.
controls.rationale: Structured content is data, not trusted executable code.
